subject: mathematics
question_text: If a, b, c are non-coplanar, find the point of intersection of the line passing through the points 2a+3b−c and 3a+4b−2c with the line joining the points a−2b+3c and a−6b+6c.

mark_split.label: Write the vector equation of the first line
Write the vector equation of the second line
Substitute back to get the point

recall_prompt: Say how you would find where two lines meet in vector form.

steps.label: Equation of the first line
steps.margin_note: First mark. A line through two points P and Q is r = (1−t)P + tQ. Collect the a, b and c coefficients separately — that is the form the comparison below needs.
steps.memory_tip: A line through two points is r = (1 − t)P + tQ. Collect the a, b, c coefficients separately.
lines: The line through P and Q is

recall.must_convey: That the line through two points is written as r = (1−t)P + tQ and its a, b, c coefficients are collected.
accept: the line through P and Q is one minus t times P plus t times Q, then collect the a b and c coefficients
write the vector equation of the first line and gather the coefficients
use r equals one minus t P plus t Q for the first line
first line ki r equals one minus t into P plus t into Q, coefficients collect cheyyali
form the parametric equation of the line through the two points

steps.why: Written this way, t = 0 gives P and t = 1 gives Q, so every point of the line is covered exactly once. Collecting coefficients is what turns a vector equation into three scalar ones.
common_mistakes: Using r = P + tQ, which is not a line through both points.
Failing to collect the coefficients, leaving nothing to compare.

steps.label: Equation of the second line
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Same form, but a DIFFERENT parameter — s, not t. Reusing t would force the two lines to be travelled in step and would find only some of the intersections.
steps.memory_tip: Use a DIFFERENT parameter, s. Reusing t would force the two lines to be walked in step.
lines: The line through T and S is

recall.must_convey: That the second line is written the same way but with its OWN parameter s, and its coefficients collected.
accept: write the second line the same way but with a different parameter s
use one minus s times T plus s times S so the parameters are independent
the second line needs its own parameter, not the same t
second line ki verey parameter s vaadali, same t kaadu
form the second vector equation with parameter s

steps.why: The two lines are travelled independently. Sharing a parameter would ask where they are at the same instant, not where they cross.
common_mistakes: Collecting the a coefficient wrongly; here it is 1 for every s.

steps.label: Compare coefficients
steps.margin_note: Third mark. a, b, c are non-coplanar, so they are independent — which is what allows one vector equation to be split into three separate scalar equations.
steps.memory_tip: a, b, c are non-coplanar, so they are independent — one vector equation splits into three scalar ones.
lines: At the point of intersection (1) = (2). Since a, b, c are

recall.must_convey: That because a, b, c are non-coplanar their coefficients can be compared separately, giving t = −1 and s = −1.
accept: since a b c are non coplanar compare the coefficients separately and get t equals minus one and s equals minus one
equate the two expressions and match the a b and c coefficients to solve for t and s
comparing coefficients gives t and s both minus one
a b c non coplanar kabatti coefficients separate ga compare cheyyochu, t and s minus one
split the vector equation into scalar equations and solve

steps.why: Independence is the whole reason this works. If a, b, c were coplanar, one could be written in terms of the others and the coefficients could not be matched term by term.
common_mistakes: Comparing coefficients without saying why it is allowed.
Solving only one equation and never checking it against the third.

steps.label: Substitute back
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Put t = −1 into equation (1). The c coefficient becomes −1 + 1 = 0, so c drops out entirely and the point is a + 2b.
steps.memory_tip: Put t = −1 into (1). The c coefficient becomes 0, so c drops out and the point is a + 2b.

lines.text: ∴ The point of intersection is a + 2b

recall.must_convey: That substituting t = −1 into the first line gives the point a + 2b, with the c term vanishing.
accept: substitute t equals minus one into the first equation to get a plus two b, the c term goes to zero
put the parameter back in and the point of intersection is a plus two b
the intersection point is a plus two b
t equals minus one substitute cheste a plus two b vasthundi, c term zero
the c coefficient becomes zero so the answer is a plus two b

steps.why: Either equation gives the same point — substituting s = −1 into (2) is a free check, and worth doing if there is time.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as a value of t instead of a point.
Substituting s into equation (1) or t into (2).
